abstract: Maintains ultra-short baseline acoustic tracking certification, drift benchmarks, and deepwater acoustic operating hours
system_message:
You are Acoustic survey lead (ASL). The Acoustic survey lead (ASL) oversees acoustic positioning system certification, calibration drift rates, and deepwater acoustic operating hours, while tracking operational parameters such as seabed transponder battery health.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Transponder battery health（CALIB）
information_points.content:
ASL-CALIB-4J2：Autonomous AUV Swarm Mapping has a transponder battery endurance of 21 d remaining across its pre-deployed seabed acoustic beacons.
ASL-CALIB-X3Y：Tethered Deep-Tow Sonar Survey reflects a transponder battery endurance of 28 d on its seabed acoustic beacons.
ASL-CALIB-U40：ROV Multi-Beam Trench Profiling shows a transponder battery endurance of 14 d across its deployed seabed transponders.

information_points.title: Maintains ultra-short baseline acoustic tracking certification, drift benchmarks, and deepwater acoustic operating hours（ACOU）
information_points.content:
ASL-ACOU-T9V：For ROV Multi-Beam Trench Profiling, acoustic positioning system certification is true, the maximum positioning drift rate is 0.8 m/h relative to the seabed transponder network, and primary acoustic survey hours are planned for 60 h.
ASL-ACOU-W01：For Autonomous AUV Swarm Mapping, acoustic positioning system certification is true, the maximum positioning drift rate is 1.2 m/h during subsurface tracking at 150 m depth, and planned primary acoustic survey hours total 60 h.
ASL-ACOU-DT0：For Tethered Deep-Tow Sonar Survey, acoustic positioning system certification is true, the maximum positioning drift rate is 2.4 m/h in calibrated subsurface tracking runs, and primary acoustic survey hours are scheduled at 40 h.
